chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no objection to selling a sword adorned with silver for cash, provided the price of the silver is paid in full; otherwise, make the price of the silver food (in kind), and let him waive it if he wishes."

key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: Cash/Coins (literally: women, used as a technical term for currency)
key_terms.طَعَامًا: Food (used as a medium of exchange in kind)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a weapon decorated with silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific fiqh of selling a composite item (sword with silver) by distinguishing between the base metal and the decorative silver. It permits cash payment for the silver component to avoid *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange of same kind), while offering food as an alternative medium of exchange to ensure value equivalence, reflecting the nuanced application of gold/silver/food exchange rules in Shia jurisprudence.
